name: Gray-faced Petrel
rangeDescription: Breeds on many islands, especially moutohora island and hongiora island (bay of plenty), and headlands of northern north island (new zealand); non-breeding range in deep subtropical water from tasman sea (off southeastern australia) to southern melanesian waters (southwestern pacific ocean)
description: A large, all-dark gadfly petrel found across the Tasman Sea and the temperate and subtropical southwest Pacific Ocean. Note the gray face, chin, and throat and the stout bill.

name: Von der Decken's Hornbill
rangeDescription: Ethiopia and southern somalia to kenya, northeastern uganda, and tanzania
description: A medium-sized black-and-white hornbill. Males have a mostly red bill with a yellow or white tip; females have an all-black bill.

name: Brown-chested Lapwing
rangeDescription: Range poorly known; breeds from nigeria east (probably) to northeastern democratic republic of the congo; disperses west to ghana, southward to cameroon and southern democratic republic of the congo, and eastward to western tanzania
description: Large, long-legged upland shorebird. Note the rufous above the bill and below the gray hood.

name: Chestnut-bellied Seedeater
rangeDescription: The guianas and southern venezuela to northern and central bolivia (pando to eastern cochabamba) and amazonian brazil
description: The gray-and-red seedeater of lowland Amazonia. Males are gray with chestnut throat and breast, and are unlikely to be confused with any other seedeater species in their range; females are tawny yellowish, warmer-colored than other female seedeaters in their range but still very similar.

name: Red-bellied Macaw
rangeDescription: Southeastern colombia to the guianas, trinidad, northern bolivia, and amazonian brazil
description: Small green macaw of lowland rainforest. Favors swampy areas, especially those with palm trees, which it uses for nesting.

name: Makira Dwarf-Kingfisher
rangeDescription: Makira (southeastern solomon islands)
description: A small kingfisher with deep purplish-blue upperparts and clean white underparts, a white neck spot, and bright orange legs. Bill is black.

name: White-browed Hawk
rangeDescription: Rainforest of eastern peru, northern bolivia, and southern amazonian brazil
description: Compact, black-and-white forest hawk. Short tail and broad wings give it a chunkier appearance than other interior forest raptors like forest-falcons and hawks in the genus Accipiter.

name: Guadalcanal Hooded Whistler
rangeDescription: Montane forest of guadalcanal (southeastern solomon islands)
description: A distinctive whistler of dark, dingy appearance. Body color is a dank mossy olive, with a slate-gray throat and a black cap.

name: Rwenzori Apalis
rangeDescription: Montane forest of eastern democratic republic of the congo, southwestern uganda, rwanda, and burundi
description: Slim, pretty, long-tailed member of the cisticola family that sports gray upperparts and buffy underparts with a black chest band. Common in montane forest of the Albertine Rift.

name: Asian Stubtail
rangeDescription: Breeds northeastern asia; winters to southeastern asia and taiwan
description: A well-named tiny songbird, “a head with wings,” with rather long bill, long legs, and very short tail. Long buffy supercilium is conspicuous even in the gloomy leaf litter and dense shrubbery where this minute bird lurks.

name: Olive-naped Weaver
rangeDescription: Senegal to nigeria and western cameroon; bioko
description: A medium-sized, pale-eyed weaver in which males and females are distinctly different, but both are colorful. Note olive-green back and nape and slender black mask through the eye.

name: Ochraceous-breasted Flycatcher
rangeDescription: East slope of andes of eastern peru (amazonas) to western bolivia (la paz)
description: Fairly small yellow-orange flycatcher that perches upright in humid montane forest. Olive brown above and warm yellowish orange below with white wingbars.

name: Sumatran Treepie
rangeDescription: Mountains of sumatra
description: A dapper and long-tailed inhabitant of Java’s foothill and montane forests. Warm brown overall, with a silvery nape, dark face, and jet-black wings marked with a small white patch.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: White-winged Scoter
rangeDescription: Breeds subarctic western alaska to eastern shore of james bay (east-central canada); winters aleutian islands to central california (eastern north pacific coast); and gulf of st. lawrence to new jersey
description: Large scoter, with distinctive white patch on wing. Dark chocolate-brown overall; males are darker than females and have small white mark under eye, dark knob on the bill, and pink bill tip.

name: Tanzanian Red-billed Hornbill
rangeDescription: Central and southern tanzania
description: A fairly small, slim, long-tailed hornbill. Note the red bill, the dark eye with a ring of black skin, and the heavily spotted back.

name: Red-billed Oxpecker
rangeDescription: Savanna of eastern and southern africa
description: A bulbul-sized olive-brown bird that sports a diagnostic all-red bill and a red eye surrounded by a fleshy yellow wattle. The juvenile lacks the bright bill and eye coloration.

name: Brown-capped Weaver
rangeDescription: Southeastern nigeria, southwestern cameroon, and bioko; western angola; far southern south sudan, eastern democratic republic of the congo, western and eastern uganda, western kenya, western rwanda, western burundi, and western tanzania
description: Unusual and attractive black-and-yellow weaver. Males show a brown cap and females a black one.

name: Red-naped Sapsucker
rangeDescription: Southwestern canada to southwestern usa; winters to northern mexico and southern baja california
description: Striking medium-sized woodpecker of western North America. Long, solid white wing patch helps distinguish it from Downy and Hairy Woodpeckers.

name: Blue Cotinga
rangeDescription: Central panama to colombia, northwestern ecuador, and western venezuela
description: Striking cotinga found from eastern Panama to northwest Ecuador. Male is deep sky blue with a dark purple throat and belly and mostly black wings.

name: Chestnut-bellied Mountain Tanager
rangeDescription: East slope of the andes of peru (la libertad to puno) and bolivia (la paz to western santa cruz)
description: Striking bicolored tanager from high elevations. Reddish orange below, blue above, with a black mask and a whitish crown and mustache.
